title: Homemade Vegetarian Chili
description: The smoky, complex flavor of this simple vegetarian chili comes from basic pantry ingredients, vegetables and spices! It makes great leftovers, too. Recipe yields 4 large or 6 moderate servings of chili.

ingredients.name: large can (28 ounces) or 2 small cans (15 ounces each) diced tomatoes**, with their juices
ingredients.raw: 1 large can (28 ounces) or 2 small cans (15 ounces each) diced tomatoes**, with their juices

ingredients.name: (15 ounces each) black beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15 ounces each) black beans, rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) pinto beans, rinsed and drained
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) pinto beans, rinsed and drained

ingredients.name: chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for garnishing
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for garnishing

ingredients.name: sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar or lime juice, to taste
ingredients.raw: 1 to 2 teaspoons sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar or lime juice, to taste

ingredients.name: Garnishes: chopped cilantro, sliced avocado, tortilla chips, sour cream or crème fraîche, grated cheddar cheese, etc.
ingredients.raw: Garnishes: chopped cilantro, sliced avocado, tortilla chips, sour cream or crème fraîche, grated cheddar cheese, etc.

steps.text: In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, warm {i1} until shimmering. Add the chopped {i2}, {i3}, carrot, {i5} and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Stir to combine and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the onion is translucent, about 7 to 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, {i8}, {i9}, {i10} and {i11}. Cook until fragrant while stirring constantly, about 1 minute.

Add the diced tomatoes and {i12}, the drained black beans and pinto beans, vegetable broth and {i16}. Stir to combine and let the mixture come to a simmer. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally and reducing heat as necessary to maintain a gentle simmer, for 30 minutes.

Remove the chili from the heat and discard {i16}. For the best texture and flavor, transfer 1 1/2 cups of the chili to a blender, making sure to get some of the liquid portion. Securely fasten the lid and blend until smooth (watch out for hot steam), then pour the blended mixture back into the pot. (Or, you can blend the chili briefly with an immersion blender, or mash the chili with a potato masher until it reaches a thicker, more chili-like consistency.)

Add the chopped cilantro, stir to combine, and then mix in the vinegar, {i18}. Add salt to taste, too—I added 1/4 teaspoon more at this point. Divide the mixture into individual bowls and serve with garnishes of your choice. This chili will keep well in the refrigerator for about 4 days or you can freeze it for longer-term storage.
